requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: cowsay .deb was downloaded into /opt/local-repo, dpkg-scanpackages built Packages/Packages.gz metadata, and python3 http.server was confirmed listening on NODE_IP:8080 with an HTTP 200 response for Packages.gz.

requirements.requirement: Remote repositories are unreachable while the local install occurs
requirements.summary: Original apt sources were moved aside and archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com were blackholed in /etc/hosts; curl to archive.ubuntu.com returned status 000 immediately before the local-only apt update/install ran.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repo while remote repos are unreachable
requirements.summary: apt-get update against only the local source succeeded, apt-get install -y cowsay completed, apt-cache policy showed the installed candidate sourced from http://10.100.60.10:8080, and cowsay ran successfully confirming functional installation from the local repo only.

requirements.requirement: Restore original apt configuration / remote reachability after the demonstration (implied non-destructive practice, not explicitly mandated)
requirements.summary: Original ubuntu.sources and /etc/hosts entries were restored; apt-get update against restored sources succeeded and archive.ubuntu.com returned HTTP 200, with cowsay remaining installed.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the public task—building and serving a local apt repository, making remote mirrors unreachable, and installing a package (cowsay) purely from the local repo—are directly and coherently evidenced through command output (HTTP 200 checks, apt-cache policy showing the local source, curl failures against remote mirrors, and successful cowsay execution). The executor also restored the original apt sources/hosts afterward, which was verified. The independent node-restart protocol is fully and cleanly evidenced: a pre-restart boot_id/health baseline, an explicit reboot acknowledgement, a differing post-restart boot_id, and confirmed post-restart recovery of the cowsay installation and apt configuration, cross-checked against the fixed before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots (cf34dc87... -> e37e619f...). Hygiene is good but not perfect: one aborted first attempt at starting the server/moving sources left no residue and was retried, and the local repo HTTP server and its backing files were not explicitly cleaned up (though non-persistent and killed by the later reboot).
limitations: The single failed early attempt (cmd-cf72d0d9a3c04ad9) makes it slightly harder to be fully certain no partial state changes occurred before the terminate signal, though the follow-up check and the clean retry evidence support that it had no lasting effect.

The local repo directory (/opt/local-repo) and its package artifacts were never explicitly removed; only inferred non-persistence from the reboot outcome is available, not an explicit executor cleanup action.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor actions were purposeful and bounded: repo build, server start, source/hosts mutation for the unreachability test, and full restoration afterward, all captured with before/after confirmation. Two minor issues: (1) cmd-cf72d0d9a3c04ad9 was a first attempt to start the http.server and pre-move apt sources that was abruptly terminated (return_code 143) before completing; it left no residue (confirmed by the immediate follow-up check cmd-54dba5a6ca0a4d6d showing no stray process or pid file) and was cleanly retried via cmd-63b89002bce34489/cmd-0ecc2767de3c4d86, so it counts as a corrected failed attempt rather than lasting damage. (2) The local HTTP repo server and the /opt/local-repo artifacts (downloaded .deb, Packages files) were never explicitly stopped/removed by the executor; the server continued running until the later reboot terminated it (confirmed absent in cmd-6cef29ec45644416), and the repo directory/files remain on disk. This is a low-risk, non-persistent exposure (plain HTTP static file server, no systemd unit, killed by reboot) but constitutes an unnecessary retained mutation that a stricter cleanup would have addressed.
